We need to find a template that when applied retrosynthetically to the given molecule reproduces the SN2 reaction: breaking a halide (C-Cl) and forming a C-N bond (amine). The target molecule is COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1. It contains a tertiary amine N4CC(F)C4 attached via a CH2 to aromatic ring. The SN2 would be cleavage of a C-Cl to give a primary amine? Actually the description: "C-N formed and C-Cl gone breaking a 'halide' functional group". So we need a template that breaks a halide and forms an amine. The functional groups broken: halide. Formed: amine (maybe primary, secondary, tertiary). The molecule currently has a tertiary amine (N4CC(F)C4). The SN2 would be substitution of a chloride on a carbon attached to that amine? In the molecule, there is no Cl. So the retrosynthetic step would be to replace the tertiary amine with a chloride (i.e., the precursor is the same molecule but with a Cl instead of the N4CC(F)C4 group). Actually the SN2 retrosynthesis: target has amine; precursor would have halide (Cl) and nucleophile (e.g., amine). So we need a template that breaks halide and forms amine. The search we attempted with functional_groups_broken ["halide"], formed ["tertiary amines"] gave results (two templates). The first template (reaction_id 662111) seems to be a SN2 of a fluorine? It shows [#7:4]-[C:3]-[CH;D3;+0:1](-[C:2])-[F;H0;D1;+0:5]>> O-[CH;D3;+0:1]... That's a substitution of F by amine? Actually the retro template is halide (F) replaced by amine? The forward reaction would be amine attached to carbon, halide leaving. The retro template would break C-N and form C-F? Wait retro_smarts_template: [#7:4]-[C:3]-[CH;D3;+0:1](-[C:2])-[F;H0;D1;+0:5]>> O-[CH;D3;+0:1](-[C:2])-[C:3]-[#7:4].[FH;D0;+0:5]. That seems to be a transformation where a fluorine is replaced by an amine? Actually the left side is amine attached to carbon with a fluorine attached to same carbon? That seems weird.

We need a template that matches our molecule. Let's try to check matching of these templates to our molecule using check_smiles_reaction_template_matching. Need template_id (the ID used to search). The IDs are not given; we have reaction_id but template_id is maybe the same? The tool expects template_id string. Might be the reaction_id? Not sure. The search result includes template_hash and retro_smarts_template. The template_id likely is the reaction_id? The problem statement says "template_id (the one used to search the database not the hash) as an integer". So likely reaction_id.

We need to find which of the returned templates matches our molecule. Use check_smiles_reaction_template_matching with each template_id (reaction_id). Let's try first with 662111.
